meta.title: Who really said "The way to get started is to quit talking and begin doing"? | Quotle.info
meta.description: Walt Disney really did say this — nearly. It traces to a July 1957 Hedda Hopper interview about financing; the popular wording is a trimmed paraphrase.
meta.ogTitle: Who really said 'The way to get started is to quit talking and begin doing'?
meta.ogDescription: Genuinely Disney's — from a July 1957 Hedda Hopper interview, where he said 'I found the way to get started was to quit talking and begin doing it.'

answer.label: Attributed to
answer.sourceLine: Widely — and, unusually for a feel-good internet quote, correctly — credited to Disney. It traces to a July 1957 interview with Hollywood columnist Hedda Hopper, in which Disney said “I found the way to get started was to quit talking and begin doing it” while describing how he pressed ahead without bank financing. The famous one-liner is a lightly trimmed paraphrase of that documented statement, so the attribution is sound even though the exact popular wording is not verbatim.

source.excerpt: I didn’t have the money to get this thing going, but I found the way to get started was to quit talking and begin doing it.
trail: Snopes traces the line to a July 1957 interview of Disney by columnist Hedda Hopper ↗, in which he said “I found the way to get started was to quit talking and begin doing it” — and rates the attribution as substantially authentic.

The polished aphorism — “The way to get started is to quit talking and begin doing” — is the version circulated on quote sites such as Goodreads ↗ and Disney’s own social channels, trimmed from Disney’s first-person original.
Notably, the quote does not appear in any sourced, attributed, or disputed section of Disney’s Wikiquote page ↗, so the 1957 Hopper interview remains the earliest documented origin.
source.excerptNote: Disney was recalling how he launched his ventures without waiting on bank credit — a specific business-financing context that the modern motivational meme drops entirely.

author.heading: About Walt Disney
author.metaLine: 1901–1966 · American animator, film producer & studio co-founder
author.bio: Walt Disney (1901–1966) was an American animator, film producer, and entrepreneur who co-founded The Walt Disney Company with his brother Roy in 1923. He pioneered the animated feature with Snow White and the Seven Dwarfs (1937), created Mickey Mouse, opened Disneyland in 1955, and won a record 22 competitive Academy Awards. His early career was marked by financial struggle and gambles made without secured funding — the very experience behind this quote.

misattribution.heading: What actually happened
misattribution.intro: This is not a case of the wrong person — Disney really did say essentially this. The distortion is subtler: the wording was smoothed and the original meaning stripped away.

items.why: Disney’s documented words were first-person and past-tense — “I found the way to get started was to quit talking and begin doing it” — per Snopes ↗. The meme form recasts it as a timeless imperative, dropping “I found” and “it” and shifting to the present tense.
Disney was describing how he pushed his ventures forward without waiting for bank credit, not offering generic life advice; Snopes ↗ notes this financing context is absent from modern uses.

misattribution.truthLine: The attribution is sound: Disney genuinely voiced this idea in a July 1957 Hedda Hopper interview ↗ — the popular version just tidies his words and forgets he was talking about money.

context.heading: Why it resonates
lead: The line endures because it compresses Disney’s entire biography — a career built on launching before the money, the studio, or the certainty was in place — into six blunt words. Stripped of its 1957 banking context, it reads as universal permission to stop deliberating and act.
That universality is also why it travels so well and why the original financing story vanished: the phrase works as pure motivation without it.
detailsBody: Disney’s recorded statement — “I didn’t have the money to get this thing going, but I found the way to get started was to quit talking and begin doing it” — is a memory of a specific business decision. The aphorism it spawned keeps the punch and discards the particulars, which is typical of how first-person anecdotes harden into quotable maxims.
